synopsis: Samak et al.’s GVSETS 2024 work is cited as an off-road digital-twin example alongside a separate construction-vehicle twin from 2025 [f399]. At GVSETS in August 2024, they reported running vision-guided AEB across 128 simulated off-road test cases using the open-source AutoDRIVE framework and high-performance computing clusters [f467, f4104]. The cluster-based approach addresses the inability of sequential parameter sweeps to explore large variability spaces under time constraints [f4104]. For virtual-job-site planning, the work supports a scaling methodology rather than prescribing a particular scenario count; the reported 128 cases should therefore not be treated as a required validation target [f4105, f467].

relations.note: Adds the framework, test count, and computing infrastructure to the cited example.
Adds the August date and rationale for using high-performance computing clusters.
The parameter-sweep limitation explains why the work supports scaling methodology.
Clarifies that the reported 128 cases do not prescribe a scenario-count target.
